videos.script: For thirty years, monitoring meant asking. Every five minutes, a server asked each router how many bytes it had counted. {{polling}} Between two questions, nobody knew anything. A link could go down and come back, and the graph would never show it. {{gap}} Streaming telemetry turns that round. You subscribe once, and the router sends the values, every two seconds, or only when something changes. {{stream}} The protocol is gNMI. It runs over gRPC, and it reads the same kind of model-shaped data as NETCONF. {{gnmi}} In this lesson you ask a router what it can serve, and read values by their path. You subscribe to a counter and turn it into a rate, while one branch pings the other. {{rate}} You watch a link go down and come back, and see exactly two messages arrive. {{onchange}} And you change a description with a Set, and read it back from the router's own CLI. {{set}}
